record.summary: Draft law that the Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST) put to public consultation from 14 April to 14 May 2025 to attract investment in data centres and AI. It aims to make the Kingdom a global digital hub and to enable sovereign data centres that ensure service continuity and data sovereignty beyond borders. It sets three models: a 'Private Center' for countries around the world to host their data and services in the Kingdom, and an 'Extended Center' and a 'Virtual Center' for major AI and cloud computing companies to host their worldwide customers in the Kingdom at levels of sovereignty and privileges suited to those customers.
record.notes: Published for public comment from 14 April to 14 May 2025 through the Public Consultation Platform, with inquiries to CST. CST states that the law aligns with relevant international treaty frameworks and principles.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: CST's news release of 14 April 2025 in English (snapshot of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 18 Oct 2026) and in Arabic (18 Oct 2026). They confirm the English and Arabic titles, CST as issuer, the consultation window and the three centre models; the summary now rests on them alone. The draft text on the Istitlaa consultation platform (secondary_url) is not stored: the platform timed out for the archiver on 11 and 18 Oct 2026. The previous summary's account of guest countries, designated foreign states and Council of Ministers approval and termination powers, and the entry into force 60 days after publication in the Official Gazette, rested on law-firm summaries and is not repeated. No stored source shows adoption, a royal decree or publication in the Official Gazette, so the record stays a draft.
